title: Ramashray Dubey v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
coram: Dilip Gupta, J.; Siddhartha Varma, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; petitioner left to Clause 6.5 remedy.
headnote: A consumer aggrieved by an electricity bill, who sought a mandamus to decide a representation without identifying the provision under which it was filed, was left to the statutory remedy under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
facts: Ramashray Dubey, who had been given an electric connection by U.P. Power Corporation Limited, was aggrieved by a bill issued for electricity consumed. He filed a representation before the respondent-authorities and approached the Allahabad High Court seeking a direction that the representation be decided. Counsel for the petitioner could not identify the provision of law under which the representation had been filed.

holding_units.holding: Where a consumer challenges an electricity bill by a representation whose statutory basis is not shown, the High Court will not direct the licensee to decide that representation; the consumer is to avail the statutory remedy under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

not_decided.point: correctness of the impugned electricity bill
not_decided.note: Not examined on merits; petitioner left to Clause 6.5.
